found_by: Agent 8 (independent auditor); re-measured independently by the lead before acting

defect.shape: the M10 defect repeating on the INPUT side
defect.statement: scripts/export_graph_world.py selects MATCH (n) WHERE NOT n:Internal -- every public label -- while the two world consumers between them declared 5 labels and 5 predicate types. graph_quality_scorecard.py reads MATCH (n) and every predicate while declaring 3 labels.

lead_measurement.note: Agent 8 reported 89.9% of exported node ROWS; the lead measured 39.0% of distinct NODES reachable by any declared label. Both measure the same defect; the lead's is the more conservative and is the figure used.

defect.consequence: every closure landing this sprint would have read CURRENT while the bundle a browser downloads was stale

fix.change: CONSUMER_SUBGRAPHS declares the subgraph a whole-subgraph reader actually reads, as a Cypher predicate, and subgraph_fingerprint() hashes node identities, a per-label census, and typed endpoint pairs over it.
fix.why_a_predicate_not_a_longer_list: an enumerated label list is correct only until the next label is added, which is precisely how this defect arose
fix.no_apoc: the compose file requires nothing in the pipeline depend on APOC, so the label census is computed as a census rather than by sorting each node's labels in Cypher
fix.second_fix: main() returned 0 unconditionally, so STALE_INPUT=5 still exited 0 and anything wired on the exit code caught nothing. --status now returns 1 on any STALE_INPUT or unexplained stale; --record deliberately still returns 0.

measured_after.expected: the three subgraph consumers are stale because a new input key is by definition moved; Wave D rebuilds and re-records them

tests.key_proof: the first test reproduces the M10 shape exactly -- a node marked :Internal, identity and edges untouched -- which an identity digest alone cannot see and which actually shipped 28 malformed metre names to every reader
